title: Does Watching Leafs vs Habs Change Your Hormones?
description:
Does watching sports change your hormones? Leafs vs Habs is tonight, and a study of World Cup fans found testosterone rose most in the tight, tense stretches. Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix before puck drop.

Researchers collected about 2,000 saliva samples from 82 soccer fans watching their national team at the 2014 World Cup. Testosterone climbed the most during close, competitive stretches and went back to baseline once a win was certain. A smaller exploratory study of 26 combat athletes watching a teammate compete found the response depended on how central the team was to their identity. Neither study looked at hockey fans, and neither says hormones make fans aggressive.

Sources (PubMed):
Burk, Mayer & Wiese, Physiol Behav 2019 — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physbeh.2019.112596
Casto et al., Hum Nat 2021 — https://doi.org/10.1007/s12110-021-09407-7

Not medical advice. AI-generated animation and voice, script and science checked by the creator.
